sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 09.10.2023.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 09.10.2023 at about 10.20 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing No. KA-13-EX-9132 along with one Vijaykumar as a rider from Nagayya Koppalu towards Shravanabelagola, near Library Mysore road,
Shravanabelagola town, Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan, he hit the wooden log which was lying on the middle of the said road by riding the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and rider both fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was initially was taken to Government Hospital at Shravanabelagola, after first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Punya Hospital, Channarayapattana wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and took treatment for severe head injury.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 34 years, working as Welder and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner lost his income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1 - insured/owner has not appeared before the tribunal, hence he has been placed exparte.
After service of summons, the respondents No.2- insurer has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
The respondent No.2- Reliance General insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the cause and manner of accident.

Further it has denied the issuance of policy to the alleged offending motor cycle bearing No. KA-13-EX-9132, in favour of first respondent and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has contended that rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid and effective driving licence to rode the same as on the date of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the alleged motorcycle in the accident.
Further by denying the age, occupation, income of the petitioner this respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

sentences.text: As per the records the accident was occurred on 09.10.2023 at about 10.20 p.m. and the FIR was registered on 10.10.2023 at about 12.30 p.m. which shows that the next date of the accident the FIR was registered.

In this regard the petitioner summoned and produced Ex.P23 and P24 MLC register extract and police intimation which shows that the petitioner admitted to Punya Hospital on 09.10.2023 while traveling in the motorcycle.
Thereby the MLC register extract and police intimation helped the petitioner to show that the petitioner sustained injuries in a RTA dated 09.10.2023.
Thereby, no grounds are made out to look the case of the petitioner suspiciously.
17. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 09.10.2023 which was caused by the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-EX- 9132 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the rider of the vehicle of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 22 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P10 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 09.01.2001.
The accident was took place on 09.10.2023.
Hence as per Ex.P.10 as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 22 years 9 months.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P9.

As per Ex.P9 the petitioner was admitted to Punya hospital from 09.10.2023 to 10.10.2023 and at SSM Multispeciality Hospital, Hassan from 10.10.2023 to 17.10.2023 and he has sustained Head injury EDH and took treatment.

By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.50,000/-
may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P11 amounting to Rs.1,82,182/- and the said bills are supported with medical prescriptions and advance receipts at Ex.P.12 & P13.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.1,83,000/-.

In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P7 - the petitioner was admitted to Punya hospital, Channarayapattana and SSM Multispeciality Hospital, Hassan for 9 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 4 months period including 9 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,000 X 4 months = Rs.64,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao, Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bengaluru as PW.2, through him OPD records, X-ray skull report, CT brain report, neuro psychological assessment report, MMSE report, CR Scan film, X-ray are marked at Ex.P15 to Ex.P.21.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained head injury.
Further it is stated that Petitioner had a GCS of E3V4M5 (12/15).

CT brain reveals left basi frontal contusion, left posterior temporal contusion,
right temporo parietal extradural hematoma, along with fractures of right parietal and right temporal bones.

Petitioner was subsequently admitted and treated at SSM Multi Speciality Hospital,
Hassan from 10/10/2023.
He had a GCS of E2M5V2.
Petitioner underwent right fronto temporal craniotomy and evacuation of extradural hematoma on 10/10/2023.
Following the injury, he has not been able to attend to his earlier work as a welder.
He complains of frequent headaches and giddiness.
He also complains of impaired memory and intelligence.
Examination revealed a conscious ambulant patient with a surgical scar on right side of his head.
He has impaired memory and intelligence.
Skull X Ray done on 11/03/2025.
This revealed right posterior temporal craniotomy.
Bone flap seen in situ.
CT Brain done on 11/03/2025.
This revealed features of left temporal gliosis.
There were also features of right posterior temporal craniotomy.
Bone flap was seen in situ.
A bone flap is a section of skull removed during a craniotomy to access the brain for surgery, or during a decompressive craniectomy to relieve intracranial pressure.
Neuro Psychological Assessment was done on 11/03/2025.
His IQ was 93 (90-110).
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered permanent disability to whole body at 10%.
On clinical observation, the PW.2 found that the petitioner has not been able to resume work as a Welder.
Petitioner complains of frequent headaches, giddiness and impaired memory.
Further PW2 found that conscious ambulant patient with surgical scar over right side head.
The PW.2 doctor is cross-examined at length by the learned counsel for the respondent.
No doubt that the PW.2 is not a treated doctor but assessed the disability of neurological assessment by using DGHS guidelines of Indian Phsyciatric association.
Nothing been elicited to disbelieve the case of the petitioner at the time of cross examination of PW.2.
But when the petitioner can answer the fact of accident in a proper and accurate way, whether the evidence of Pw.2 regarding the cognitive disability can be considered or not has to be looked into.
No doubt that the petitioner's normal life is disturbed by the accident.
But as per the evidence of PW.2 doctor in the complex situation the petitioner cannot behave normally and he is suffering with frequent head aches and impaired memory.

sentences.text: The total body disability disability of the petitioner is assessed at 10%.
As per Ex.P18 neurological assesment report the petitioner suffering with mild disability.
It is stated that the petitioner was working as Welder but no evidence is placed in this regard.
By considering the nature of the work of the petitioner certainly the disability caused by the injuries sustained in the accident it may effect the working capacity of the petitioner.
Hence the functional disability of the petitioner by considering the alleged nature of work is assessed at 10%.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '18'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 18 X 10% =Rs.3,45,600/- which is the total loss of future income.
d) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P9 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 9 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the injury sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.35,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
e) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 9 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

By considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.9,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 9 days in the hospital.
f) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
h) Future Medical Expenses: PW.2 has not stated that the petitioner needs surgery in future.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: Liability:- The respondent No.2 is the insurer, respondent No.1 is the owner of Motorcycle bearing No. KA-13-EX-9132.
Even though in the written statement the respondent No.2 denied the issuance of policy in the offending vehicle has not produced any documents to prove the same.
No evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,26,600/- (Rupees Seven lakhs twenty six thousand six hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondent No.1.
The respondent No.2- insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
